reasons: Status 'missing' is credible on the record supplied: the excerpts and the rationale's survey of the nearby provisions (5.2 editorial control, 5.3 merchant-of-record, 6.1 limited Marks licence with no implied licences, 8 confidentiality, 10.2 no co-ownership) show no ownership or assignment clause covering the Site, deliverables, Content or customer data, and no licence back of HDI platform IP.

The inserted Section 5.5 reaches the preferred position with a single, self-contained addition: Company ownership of the Site/deliverables/customer data plus HDI assignment, HDI retention of its pre-existing software and tools, a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense embedded HDI materials, and an express no-joint-ownership / no-assignment-to-HDI backstop. Directionally correct for the Customer and not an over-flag of an acceptable fallback.

Placement and numbering are sensible (appended after the Section 5.4 General Manager paragraph, before the Section 6 Marks licence), and the deterministic checks confirm no residual assignment of Customer IP or data to HDI.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice, and correctly frames the change (we own what we pay for and put in; HDI keeps its pre-existing platform with a licence back) without lecturing.

Minor, non-blocking: confirm the final section number against the executed Section 5 sequence, and that the broad claim to ownership of 'the Site' (rather than only the Content, deliverables and data) does not conflict with any revenue-share or hosting-platform provisions elsewhere in the Agreement.
